description: n512 B640 marquee shape: the blocked-Householder trailing apply (qr_panel_apply_fused) is 51% of runtime, a panel-sequential chain. Replace the well-conditioned subset's path with batched CholeskyQR2 (G=A^T A, Cholesky R, Q=A R^{-1}, repeated once for orthogonality), done entirely in BF16/TF32 tensor-core batched GEMMs with FP32 accumulate, then recover the compact Householder (H,tau) via orhr_col-style Householder reconstruction. Keep the per-matrix ill-conditioned geqrf fallback. Target turning the sequential panel chain into 3 big batched GEMMs the B200 tensor cores saturate.

n512 B640: the blocked-Householder trailing update (qr_panel_apply_fused, 51%) is the bottleneck and runs FP16. Drop its bulk GEMMs (V^T C and V(T^T W)) to FP8 e4m3 with per-tile/amax scaling and FP32 accumulate on the tcgen05 tensor cores, then restore FP32 orthogonality with one Newton-Schulz or Gram-Schmidt reortho pass on the affected columns. Keep panel factor + T-factor in FP32/BF16. Per-matrix demote to the existing path where FP8 amax indicates overflow/ill-conditioning. Goal: ~2x the dominant GEMM throughput vs FP16.

n4096 B2 (11222us, single biggest shape) and n2048 B8: the CholeskyQR path uses an UNBATCHED per-matrix FP64 cholesky loop, and B200 FP64 is weak; with only 2-8 matrices the GPU is massively occupancy-starved (148 SMs idle). Restructure to a multi-CTA-per-matrix tensor-core blocked QR: split each large matrix across many CTAs so all 148 SMs are busy, do the O(n^3) trailing updates in BF16/TF32 batched GEMMs with FP32 accumulate, and reconstruct compact (H,tau) via the existing orhr_col-style path. Eliminate the FP64 loop.

n1024 B60 (shapes 4/8/11, ~3300us each): the large-n two-level blocked path is panel-sync/latency-bound (panel ~53%). Widen the outer block and route the trailing update through tcgen05 tensor-core GEMMs (BF16 storage, FP32-V reflectors for orthogonality), cutting the number of panel barriers and the per-panel GEMV-like work. Reduce panel passes so the bulk O(n^3) work lands on saturated tensor-core GEMMs rather than the latency-bound panel chain.

Mixed-batch n512 shape 7 (5084us, slowest 512) and n1024 mixed shape 8: ill-conditioned matrices in the mixed batch fall back to per-matrix torch.geqrf, which serializes and dominates. Replace the fallback with a batched accurate GPU path for the ill-conditioned subset: shifted-CholeskyQR (add a small mu*I shift to make A^T A+muI positive-definite, then CholeskyQR2 + one step of iterative refinement) or batched column-pivoted panel, so ill-conditioned matrices stay on a batched tensor-core path instead of looping cuSOLVER. Cut the geqrf scatter cost.

n512 B640: fuse panel-factor + trailing-apply into one persistent warp-specialized megakernel in CUDA C++/CUTE DSL on sm_100a. Use a producer/consumer split (TMA/async-copy warps stage panel and trailing tiles into SMEM while tcgen05 MMA warps consume), software-pipelined across outer blocks, so the whole n512 QR for a CTA's matrices runs in a single launch with no global round-trips between panel and trailing GEMM. Attacks the 51% qr_panel_apply launch-and-reload overhead directly.

n512 B640 GOOD (well-conditioned) subset, the 51% qr_panel_apply_fused trailing update currently runs FP16 + needs FP32 reortho cleanup. Forking off the brief-4 best (which proved cuBLAS-13 BF16x9 FP32-emulation is bit-FP32-exact and leaderboard-portable on this kernel): route the n512 GOOD-subset trailing block-reflector GEMMs (V^T C, V(T^T W)) through BF16x9 emulation instead of FP16. BF16x9 is FP32-exact, so this should match accuracy WITHOUT the FP16 path's fixup passes (classify_convert 5.4%, fill_R_zero_tail 2.8%) while still using tensor cores. Compare BF16x9 vs the current FP16+cleanup end-to-end on shape 3.

n512 PAF kernel (qr_panel_apply_fused, 51%) is OCCUPANCY/BARRIER-bound per ncu: CTA-barrier stalls 34-39%, only ~2 CTA/SM (96KB SMEM), tensor pipe ~45% idle, NOT MMA-bound. Raise occupancy and cut barrier stalls: shrink the 96KB SMEM footprint (smaller staged tiles / drop redundant SMEM buffers / reuse) to fit 3-5 CTA/SM so the scheduler hides barrier latency, and reduce the number of __syncthreads per outer block (fuse phases, double-buffer, or async-copy pipeline so fewer full-CTA barriers). Goal: more concurrent CTAs to overlap the barrier-stall bubbles, attacking the 51% kernel at its real bottleneck.

Small shapes s0 n32 (10us), s1 n176 (251us), s2 n352 (592us) are UNATTACKED and each is 1/12 of the geomean — equal weight to n4096, so halving s1/s2 helps geomean as much as halving n4096. They are launch/overhead-bound (many small kernel launches + Python dispatch + per-shape flag-setting). Attack the launch overhead: capture each small-shape path as a CUDA graph and replay (eliminating per-launch + Python overhead across the timed reps), and raise the n176 megakernel / n352 bf16 occupancy so more matrices run per wave. Also profile to see if the n352 bf16 two-level path can widen its block to cut launches. Goal: cut the 3 small shapes' overhead-dominated time.

n512 B640 dominant shape spends ~16% on NON-math support kernels no worker touches: classify_convert_n512 (5.4%, one 167us launch that FP32->FP16 converts + classifies good/bad), build_Minv_blk4 (8%, the T-factor inverse), fill_R_zero_tail_n512 (2.8%, 85us zeroing R's sub-diagonal). These are format/bookkeeping, gate-safe (no accuracy risk). Fuse and shrink them: merge classify+convert into the panel's first load (convert on the fly), fold fill_R_zero_tail into the apply epilogue (write zeros while writing R), and cut build_Minv cost (cheaper batched TRSM or fold into the trailing GEMM). Eliminate separate launches/passes over the B*n*n data. Hits 5/12 of geomean off the clean remote-valid baseline.

n512 PAF kernel is MEMORY-bound (58% memory SOL > 45% compute, per ncu) on top of the 31% barrier stalls. Attack the memory term with a warp-specialized cp.async/TMA SOFTWARE PIPELINE: split the CTA into a producer warp-group that stages the NEXT outer block's A/V/C tiles into SMEM via cp.async (or TMA on sm_100a) while a consumer warp-group computes the CURRENT block's panel+apply, double-buffered so global-load latency is fully hidden behind compute. Same math (gate-safe, FP16/FP32 storage unchanged), so it stays remote-valid. Distinct from the named-barrier scheduling attack: this hides MEMORY latency, not barrier bubbles. Operator-requested warp-specialization + pipelining.

n2048 B=8 (shape5, 7159us = 2nd-biggest shape) is occupancy-starved: only 8 matrices on 148 SMs on the FP16 blocked-Householder path. brief-2 flagged it as needing its own brief but never built it. Unlike n1024 (barrier-latency-bound, splitting hurts), n2048 with so few matrices is likely WORK-STARVED, so the more-CTAs fix applies: split each matrix's PARALLEL trailing apply (C-=VY) and/or the wide build_Minv across multiple CTAs/matrix to fill idle SMs (panel stays 1 CTA — serial). Profile shape5 first to confirm wave count / idle SMs and locate the dominant kernel. Stock-only ops (no BF16x9 emulation — remote-unsafe); keep comfortable factor-residual margin. Measure against clean baseline.

The block-reflector T-factor INVERSE (build_Minv_blk4) is ~8% of BOTH the n512 (build_Minv 8%) AND n1024 (7.8%) shapes = 8/12 of the geomean, and three workers flagged it but none built the fix. Replace the explicit T-inverse with a batched triangular SOLVE: instead of forming M=T^-1 and multiplying, solve T·X = (rhs) in place via stock cuBLAS strsmBatched or a custom warp/CTA TRSM. Solving is both cheaper (no explicit inverse materialization) and MORE accurate than forming the inverse, so it is gate-safe. Stock-only ops (no BF16x9 emulation - remote-unsafe). A win stacks across the two biggest shape groups. Profile build_Minv on n512 and n1024 first, then swap and measure.

Run-wide finding: the serial Householder PANEL is the universal bottleneck at every shape (trailing already optimal); the ONLY lever against it is an algorithm swap. CholeskyQR is dead for big/ill-cond (cond^2 wall + orhr_col recon tax), but the SMALL WELL-CONDITIONED shapes s1 n176 (B40, cond1) and s2 n352 (B40, cond1) are its sweet spot: small cond(A) so cond^2 fits FP32, and the orhr_col recon is cheap at small n. Replace the n176/n352 panel with batched CholeskyQR2 (G=A^T A via batched GEMM filling all SMs, batched FP32 potrf, Q=A R^-1, repeat once, then orhr_col reconstruct compact (H,tau)). Guard ill-cond inputs to the safe Householder path. Stock-only ops (no BF16x9). The bold algorithmic swing at the proven bottleneck where CholeskyQR's objections are weakest.

Householder QR has an irreducible n-column serial DEPTH (reflector j needs j-1); every panel widen/split/recurse attempt failed on this. Attack the DEPTH itself with batched-TSQR (communication-avoiding QR) on the tall panels of n4096 B2 (11222us, biggest shape) + n2048 B8: tile each tall panel into row-blocks, factor ALL tiles of BOTH matrices in ONE batched cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched (device-filling, not 1-2 CTAs), then combine the per-tile R-factors up a LOG-DEPTH reduction tree (each combine a small 2nb x nb batched QR). Reconstruct the flat geqrf-compatible compact (H,tau) from the hierarchical reflectors (the crux). Stock cuSOLVER/cuBLAS only (no emulation - remote-unsafe).

Revive brief-0's CholeskyQR2 for n512 good subset: it lost (2408us) mainly because its Gram G=A^T A was a 5.8ms FP32 SIMT GEMM (the single biggest item). Replace that Gram with an int-Ozaki INT8 tensor-core Gram - the SAME technique already used in this kernel's n4096 arm (so it is stock INT8 MMA, remote-portable, NOT a cuBLAS emulation mode). int-Ozaki decomposes FP32 into INT8 slices, does the GEMM on INT8 tensor cores, recomposes to FP32-accuracy. This attacks the dominant cost of the CQR2 path; combined with the existing tensor-core blocked TRSM + fast orhr_col recon, measure whether CQR2 (GEMM-bound, no serial Householder panel) can now beat the FP16 blocked-Householder on the n512 good subset. Stock-only; keep gate margin.

The orhr_col-style Householder RECONSTRUCTION (panel_solve_fused + diag_lu_warp) is co-dominant in two paths: ~31% of the n4096 CholeskyQR (brief-2) and ~6ms of the n512 CQR2 (brief-15) -- it is a per-panel serial LU of (Q - diag), a 2nd serial factorization. Attack it directly: multi-CTA-per-matrix and/or tensor-core the recon's panel-LU so it stops being a serial single-CTA chain. A faster recon makes BOTH the large-n CholeskyQR and the n512 int-Ozaki CQR2 viable. Profile the recon kernels first to find the dominant one, then split/tensor-core it. Stock-only (no BF16x9; OB64/IB32).

n512 PAF kernel (qr_panel_apply_fused, 51% of the dominant shape, the highest-remote-value kernel) has 58% Memory SOL dominated by SMEM BANK CONFLICTS, not DRAM (ncu: 1.4-way load / 1.5-way store conflicts, 28% excessive wavefronts, DRAM <13%). Attack the conflicts with SMEM layout/padding: pad the leading dimension of the V/C/W/reflector SMEM tiles to avoid 32-bank aliasing (e.g. +1 or +skew padding so consecutive rows/threads hit distinct banks), and reorder accesses for conflict-free swizzled load/store. Pure SMEM-layout change -> byte-identical math, gate-safe, remote-portable. Profile the PAF kernel's shared-load/store conflict counters before/after. This targets the actual mechanism behind the 58% memory term that cp.async could not touch.
